📖 Verse of the Day

"You will keep in perfect peace those whose minds are steadfast, because they trust in you."
— Isaiah 26:3

What is this verse speaking to you today? Drop your thoughts below. ✨

Today's devotional — Love Isn't Soft

"Love is patient and is kind; love doesn't envy. Love doesn't brag, is not proud." — 1 Corinthians 13:4

The world hears "love" and thinks soft — weak, a doormat. But the people who love for real are the strongest in the room. Real love costs something.

I've seen love forgive the unforgivable, stay when leaving was easier, and tell the truth when a lie would've kept the peace. That's not soft. That's steel with a heartbeat.

"Love is patient and is kind; love doesn't envy. Love doesn't brag, is not proud." Notice what's missing: feelings. Love is a verb here — patient, kind, humble. It's what you do, not what you feel.

God didn't love you because you were lovable. He loved you at your worst. That's the standard — and it's the love He's pouring into you so you can pour it into people who don't deserve it. Like the ones who did it to you.

Pick the hardest person in your life and do one patient, kind thing for them today — not for them, but for the love God put in you. Love isn't soft. It's the strongest thing there is.

Read the full devotional and listen to today's verse at /devotionals.

Today's devotional — Seek Him First

"Seek the LORD and his strength. Seek his face forever." — 1 Chronicles 16:11

Seek the LORD and His strength — in that order. Most of us want the strength without the seeking. We want the power, the breakthrough, the blessing, but we'd rather skip the face-to-face part. It doesn't work that way.

His strength, not yours. You've been trying to muscle through in your own power and calling it faith. Real faith seeks HIS strength — which means admitting yours ran out. That's not failure. That's the starting line.

Seek His face forever. Not His hand — His face. Don't just chase what He gives. Chase who He is. The gifts are great, but the Giver is better. Forever means this isn't a phase. It's a lifestyle.

Seeking is active. It's not waiting for God to show up while you scroll. It's opening the Word, it's praying first, it's choosing Him in the morning before the world gets its vote.

Seek Him today — His face, His strength — and watch what happens to everything else you're chasing. It either falls into place or falls away. Both are mercy.

Read the full devotional and listen to today's verse at /devotionals.

🙌 Testimony Tuesday

It's Testimony Tuesday — and we want to hear what God has done in your life.

Share a recent moment where you saw God show up. Big or small. Fresh or years old. Every testimony builds faith in someone else.

What is your testimony this week?

Pastor Philip, Pastor Steven Furtick, Joel Osteen, Jamal Bryant — they're all just names. Men of flesh, just like me. Not one of us has stood on a mountain talking to a burning bush. LOL.

**Stop defending men more than you defend the Word of God.**

Stop putting pastors on pedestals because they have millions of followers, massive churches, bestselling books, or sold-out tours. A large congregation doesn't automatically mean a ministry is aligned with God's heart.

When did ministry become about building a brand instead of building the Kingdom? When did it become about buying my book, attending my podcast tour, supporting my platform, or celebrating how many people I can get into a building?

**Money was never supposed to be the purpose. Souls were.**

I'm not saying a pastor shouldn't earn a living. I'm asking when the mission became secondary to the money.

And why are we so afraid to speak the truth? Pastors walking on eggshells, afraid to offend people, afraid to lose followers, afraid to challenge the very hearts they're supposed to shepherd.

We've got sheep beginning to look like goats, being fed by people who sometimes seem more interested in feeding their own agendas than feeding God's flock.

And let's stop dividing the body of Christ into labels. Black church. White church. Mega church. Small church.

**Since when did Jesus belong to a demographic?**

God didn't call us to build celebrity fan clubs. He called us to love, serve, forgive, restore, and reach the lost.

Jesus spoke about leaving the ninety-nine to find the one. THE ONE!

The broken one. The forgotten one. The person who can't afford your conference ticket. The person who will never buy your book. The person sitting alone, crying, wondering whether God even hears them.

That's the person I want my ministry to reach.

And before anyone misunderstands me, I'm not claiming to be better than any of these pastors. I'm a man of flesh, too. I fall short. I make mistakes. I need God's grace every single day.

But I refuse to confuse popularity with anointing, wealth with wisdom, or a microphone with a calling.

**Go back to your Bible. Not for a sermon to impress somebody. Not for a quote to get likes. Go back and ask God what needs to change in YOUR heart.**

I'm glad churches are filling seats. I'm glad people are showing up.

But here's my question:

**How many people are leaving those buildings knowing Jesus better, and how many are leaving simply admiring the person holding the microphone?**

Because at the end of the day, nobody needs my autograph.

They need Jesus.

**16:3 Faith — Proverbs 16:3**

*Commit your works to the Lord, and your thoughts shall be established.*

**Less celebrity. More Christ. Less agenda. More souls.** 🙏🏾

We should live our lives being who God wants us to be. Remember we are not billboards, but we do our own advertising by the way we live our lives. People will see you for who you really are. They hear your words and see your actions. We are to live so that Jesus can be seen in us. Remember that you do your own advertising and there's always someone watching you. God created us in His own image! People are always watching to see if they can see any of God's reflections in us.

COUNT YOUR BLESSINGS.

No, seriously... count them.

You woke up today.

You opened your eyes.

Your heart is still beating.

And before you start telling me what went wrong, who left you, how much money you don't have, what bill is due, who hurt you, or what prayer hasn't been answered yet...

You are still here.

Somebody didn't wake up this morning.

Somebody went to sleep thinking they had tomorrow.

Somebody thought they had another week to apologize.

Another month to forgive.

Another year to get their life together.

Another Sunday to finally take God seriously.

They didn't.

But you did.

See, we treat another day like God owed it to us.

He didn't.

We complain because the car isn't nice enough while somebody would give anything just to drive home one more time.

We complain about our kids getting on our nerves while somebody is sitting in an empty bedroom wishing they could hear their child's voice again.

We complain about calling our parents back while somebody is staring at a contact in their phone they'll never be able to call again.

We complain about getting older while somebody begged God for another birthday.

Man... count your blessings.

You got another chance.

Another chance to say you're sorry.

Another chance to forgive.

Another chance to stop holding that grudge.

Another chance to tell somebody you love them.

Another chance to help somebody who can't help you back.

Another chance to fall on your knees and say, “Jesus, I've been doing this my way long enough.”

Because I'm going to tell you something people don't like hearing...

Tomorrow isn't promised.

And neither is another opportunity to get right with God.

Jesus said:

“For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” — Mark 8:36

Read that again.

You can have the house.

The money.

The followers.

The business.

The title.

The body.

The clothes.

The attention.

You can have everybody in the world screaming your name...

and still lose the only thing that actually mattered.

Your soul.

I'm not trying to scare you into Jesus.

I'm trying to remind you that time is moving whether you're ready or not.

So stop wasting days trying to impress people who won't be standing beside you when you meet God.

Love people.

Forgive people.

Feed somebody.

Call your mother.

Call your father.

Hug your children.

Tell somebody you're sorry.

Get out of that drama.

Put the phone down.

Open your Bible.

Go somewhere quiet.

Talk to God.

And thank Him.

Because while you're asking God for another blessing...

you might be standing inside one already.

You're breathing.

You're here.

You still have time.

You got another chance today.

Please don't waste it.

Where We Find The One.

“Commit to the LORD whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.” — Proverbs 16:3

Honestly…

When we grow, we’re supposed to become wise.

And I really wonder sometimes…

What gets into a person’s heart that makes them want to be mean?

Cruel?

Talk about somebody?

Make somebody feel small?

Because I walk by people and think…

You are beautifully made.

Seriously.

You are.

And to the one looking in the mirror tonight…

Second guessing your beauty…

Your body…

Your worth…

Wondering if anybody will ever really love you…

You are worth it.

Please understand that.

This world isn’t about me.

It’s not about how many people know my name.

It’s about helping somebody else understand that their life matters too.

The same people I hug…

Were made with intention.

The stranger I walk past…

Made with intention.

The person everybody ignores…

Made with intention.

Even the person who doesn’t like me…

Has intention.

Even my enemy.

And that’s why I can still love them.

That’s why I can forgive them.

Because carrying anger around all day is heavy.

Hate is heavy.

Bitterness is heavy.

And some of you have been carrying it so long, you forgot what it feels like to put it down.

If that’s you…

Talk to somebody.

Talk to me.

Talk to someone you trust.

But please don’t spend this beautiful life believing you are worthless.

Because you’re not.

And those things you keep calling flaws?

Your scars.

Your body.

Your smile.

Your laugh.

The things you wish you could change…

Those might be the exact things the person meant to love you looks at and says…

That’s what I love about you.

You don’t have to be everybody’s definition of beautiful.

You don’t have to be everybody’s type.

You don’t need everybody to understand you.

You just need to understand…

You have value.

So if you’re scrolling past this tonight and this kind of love bothers you…

If kindness feels like too much…

If telling somebody they’re beautiful bothers you…

If forgiving people sounds weak…

If loving your enemy sounds stupid…

Then maybe you have to ask yourself…

What’s in my heart?

Because I don’t want to live angry.

I don’t want to hate anybody.

I don’t want somebody walking away from me feeling smaller than they did before they met me.

I want the hurting person to feel seen.

I want the lonely person to feel noticed.

I want the person questioning their beauty to hear…

You are beautifully made.

And I want the person questioning whether their life matters to know…

Yes.

It does.

Whether you believe in the God I believe in or not…

I’ll still love you.

I’ll still hug you.

I’ll still remind you that you matter.

Because my Bible tells me…

“I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” — Psalm 139:14

And if God allows me to cross your path…

I hope you walk away knowing one thing…

You were seen.

We All have scars you receive in life, that will never go away. Some scars are visible, and some are carried quietly within us, but every scar tells a story of survival, strength, and grace. Recently I had 2 deadtramental experiences that I survived open heart surgery and a stroke with 2 years left me with changes I carry with me every single day. The scars remain, and so do the reminders of those difficult seasons, but so does something even greater... God's hand over my life.Twice He carried me through moments that could have ended very differently. Twice He reminded me that His plans for me were not finished. Twice He surrounded me with His mercy, His grace, and a love so deep that I can never deny His presence in my journey. There are days when I look at my scars and the challenges left behind, but instead of seeing what was taken from me, I choose to see what God gave back to me, more time, more purpose, more gratitude, and another opportunity to love the people around me. We all carry scars that may never fully disappear. Some are on our bodies, some are on our hearts, and some are hidden where no one else can see them. But scars are not proof that God abandoned us. Sometimes they are evidence that He brought us through what was meant to break us. I know beyond any doubt that God loves me very much because He has shown me His love, mercy, and grace in ways I will spend the rest of my life thanking Him for. I am still here. I am still standing. And by the grace of God, I am still moving forward. ❤️‍🩹🙏🏼

The other day, I had a conversation with a young lady. As we talked about many different things, she asked me how I started coaching and counseling people.

I explained that for as long as I can remember, people have always been drawn to me to talk. They would come seeking advice, encouragement, or simply someone who would listen. They appreciated the wisdom they received and would often refer others to me. At the time, I was not actively practicing. I simply did it because God would often tell me that someone was coming or that He was sending someone my way.

At that point in my life, I was in college studying architecture. I shared with her that after I was abducted at the age of 20, God revealed something to me. He showed me that what I had experienced would one day help save others from unnecessary pain, grief, and suffering. He made it clear that my testimony would become a source of healing and hope for those who crossed my path.

I told her that from that moment forward, whenever someone needed guidance, advice, understanding, or simply a listening ear, God would send them my way, whether I knew them or not.

Two years ago, I decided to pursue another degree. The degree itself was not what mattered most to me. What was important was adding credibility to the wisdom and knowledge I had been sharing for years. Although the lives I had touched already testified to the value of what I offered, I felt led to obtain formal credentials as well.

She then said to me, “I don’t know that God has ever called me to help people in that way.”

I smiled and explained that not everyone is called to serve in the same capacity. There are countless ways to be a blessing to others.

I shared a few examples with her. I told her she could prepare meals for those in need. She could purchase Bibles from ministries that offer them for just a few dollars, place five dollars inside each one, and put them in a bag with a blanket, a meal, and an encouraging note to give to someone struggling. She could stop and have a conversation with a person sitting alone or someone holding a sign on the side of the road. Sometimes the greatest gift we can offer is simply seeing someone and acknowledging their humanity.

As we talked, her face began to light up. You could see the excitement and purpose growing within her. She thanked me for the ideas and encouragement.

I told her not to thank me, but to thank the Father, because He was the One who brought the conversation to fruition.

She hugged me and walked away with a lighter step, carrying a renewed sense of purpose.

Thank You, Holy Spirit, for Your perfect timing.

Tonight...

I’m standing on this balcony.

16:3 Faith hoodie on.

City underneath me.

And God...

my heart is heavy.

Not broken.

Not defeated.

Just heavy.

Because I can see thousands of lights from up here...

and behind every one of those lights is a story.

send me.

don't let me change.

don't let my heart get smaller.

Money.

Tours.

Merchandise.

Platforms.

Fame.

Lord, keep reminding me:

Love doesn't need a price tag.

And nobody should have to clean themselves up before they're allowed to sit beside me.

never let my clothes become too nice to sit beside a homeless man.

Never let my hands become too busy to hug somebody.

let the crowd become more important than the one.

Because somewhere underneath all these lights...

One person who feels forgotten.

One person who feels unwanted.

One person who doesn't believe anymore.

there's a seat.

there's a seat.

Step back. Seriously, step back.

Our minds race, stress hits us, frustration builds, and before we know it, we are reacting to something that might not even deserve a reaction. We have to learn to step back before our emotions make decisions that our hearts will later regret. Emotions can make us say things we don't mean, become mean to people we love, destroy relationships we prayed for, quit things we were called to finish, and make permanent decisions during temporary moments.

Think about how crazy that is.

One bad day can make you question an entire life.

One argument can make you forget years of love.

One disappointment can make you believe God abandoned you.

One rejection can make you question your worth.

One stressful morning can change the way you speak to everybody you encounter for the rest of the day.

That's how powerful an unchecked mind can become.

But everything you feel does not deserve a response.

Everything that hurts you does not require revenge.

Every disagreement doesn't need your final word.

Every closed door isn't the end of your story.

Sometimes maturity is walking away from the phone before sending the message. Sometimes strength is sitting quietly instead of proving your point. Sometimes faith is saying, "God, I don't understand what is happening right now, so I'm going to trust You before I trust what I'm feeling."

Because feelings change.

That anger you feel right now may be gone tomorrow.

That heartbreak that feels unbearable today may eventually become the very thing you thank God for protecting you from.

That situation you're losing sleep over may look completely different a week from now.

So don't destroy tomorrow because today hurt.

Don't ruin a relationship because you had a bad hour.

Don't speak permanent words from temporary emotions.

Don't walk away from your calling because the journey became uncomfortable.

And please don't let somebody else's darkness convince you to become somebody you were never created to be.

Guard your heart.

Guard your mouth.

Guard your decisions.

There is tremendous power in being able to say, "I'm upset, but I'm not going to become ugly."

"I'm hurt, but I'm not going to hurt somebody else."

"I'm disappointed, but I'm not going to lose my character."

"I'm confused, but I'm not going to lose my faith."

"I'm angry, but anger will not become my master."

Scripture says, "Be angry, and do not sin." — Ephesians 4:26.

God never said you wouldn't feel anger. He never said you wouldn't become exhausted, disappointed, frustrated, or overwhelmed. He teaches us not to allow those emotions to control what happens next.

That's the difference.

Anybody can react.

It takes strength to respond with wisdom.

Anybody can scream.

It takes strength to remain gentle.

Anybody can hurt somebody after being hurt.

It takes healing to refuse to pass that pain forward.

So before you send it...

Before you say it...

Before you quit...

Before you walk away...

Before you allow one terrible moment to determine the direction of your entire life...

Give yourself enough time to see the situation without the emotion attached to it.

Pray.

Get quiet.

Talk to God.

And remember something extremely important:

You do not have to make a lifetime decision based on how you feel today.

Tomorrow might bring clarity.

Tomorrow might bring an apology.

Tomorrow might bring an answer.

Tomorrow might bring healing.

And sometimes tomorrow simply brings a calmer version of you who is grateful that yesterday's version didn't destroy something that mattered.

Protect that person.

Protect your tomorrow.

Because one moment can change your direction...

but wisdom can change it back.

As I sat here painting, I couldn't help but think about how much it reflects the goodness of God.
A blank canvas starts with endless possibilities, much like our lives in the hands of our Creator. A painter carefully chooses each color, each stroke, and each detail to create something beautiful. In the same way, God lovingly works in every part of our lives, even the parts that seem messy or unfinished.
Sometimes a painting looks confusing in the middle of the process. There are layers, shadows, and colors that don't seem to make sense. Yet the artist sees the finished masterpiece before anyone else does. God's goodness is like that. Even when we don't understand what He is doing, He is still painting a beautiful story with our lives.
A painting is also a reflection of the artist's heart. When I see beauty in art, I am reminded that all beauty comes from God. Every sunrise, every flower, every mountain, and every loving act reveals the creativity and goodness of our Heavenly Father.
The gift of painting is more than putting color on a canvas—it is a reminder that we were created by the greatest Artist of all. God takes broken pieces, difficult seasons, and unexpected colors and weaves them together into something far more beautiful than we could imagine.
May we never forget that the God who painted the heavens with stars and the earth with beauty is the same God who is lovingly painting His purpose into our lives every day.
"He has made everything beautiful in its time." — Ecclesiastes 3:11
Our lives are God's masterpiece, and His goodness is found in every brushstroke.

The mirror.

I checked it often when I was around you.

Not because I was vain.

Because I was trying to recognize the man looking back at me.

Pause.

I questioned myself.

I would pull back my top lip and look at where you had bloodied it.

I would look at the scratches on my arms.

The marks.

The evidence.

And still…

I never fought back.

Not because I couldn't.

Not because I wasn't strong enough.

But because these hands were never meant to hurt you.

Pause.

My name was given to me by my parents.

Jeremy.

My titles were given through the life God entrusted to me.

Dad.

Pastor.

But you gave me other names.

Loser.

Weak.

Not a real man.

And after hearing those words enough times, I started wondering if maybe you were right.

I second-guessed my worth.

I questioned my strength.

I questioned the man staring back at me in that mirror.

And as hard as this is to admit…

I wasn't strong enough to leave.

Pause.

My children begged me.

My mother looked at me and said,

“Son, she is going to kill you. And you can't fix her.”

But love…

Or at least what I thought was love…

Had blinded me.

I kept believing things would change.

I kept believing I could love enough for both of us.

I kept believing that if I prayed harder, forgave one more time, stayed a little longer, or tried a little harder, somehow everything would become okay.

But sometimes you can love somebody and still have to leave.

Sometimes forgiveness doesn't mean giving someone continued access to destroy you.

Sometimes walking away is how you finally begin walking toward God again.

Pause.

And today, I understand something about myself.

Yes, I'm a strong man.

Physically, I'm strong.

I've been through things that taught me how to survive.

But these hands?

They aren't meant to hurt.

They're meant to help.

They're meant to hug.

They're meant to hold.

They're meant to reach for somebody who has fallen and say,

“Give me your hand. I've been down there before.”

Pause.

So God…

I don't ask You to erase what happened.

I don't ask You to make me forget every night, every word, every mark, or every moment I stood in that mirror wondering what happened to me.

Instead…

Use it.

Use every scar.

Use every memory.

Use every tear.

Use every moment I questioned my worth.

Use the pain I went through, even though it happened a long time ago, to help somebody who is living through it right now.

Let the man who once couldn't find the strength to leave become the man who helps somebody else find theirs.

Let the father whose children once begged him to get away become the father who teaches his children what love should actually look like.

Let the man who was called a loser remind somebody else that another person's cruelty does not determine their value.

And let the pastor who once looked into a mirror wondering if he was worth anything stand before hurting people and tell them:

God still sees you.

God still knows your name.

And your story does not have to end where your pain began.

Pause.

I once thought I was a destroyed man.

Today, I know differently.

I was wounded.

But God healed me.

And if the scars I carry can help one person recognize that what they're experiencing isn't love…

If my testimony can help one person find the courage to seek safety…

If what tried to break me can become something God uses to help somebody else…

Then Lord,

use all of it.

The mirror doesn't show me the same man anymore.

I see a father.

I see a pastor.

I see a servant.

I see a man whose hands are still open.

And most importantly…

I see a man who survived long enough to discover that God wasn't finished writing his story.

“He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.” — Psalm 147:3

Where We Find The One.

The math is usually pretty clear when you're dealing with good versus evil.

And sometimes numbers make you see things differently.

For me, if I can reach the 1...

If I can help save the 1...

Then I did my job.

Because that's what I believe Jesus showed us.

Leave the 99.

Go find the 1.

Pause.

There are roughly 16 million Jewish people in the world today.

Revelation 7 speaks about 144,000 being sealed from the tribes of Israel.

Now do the math.

144,000 out of 16 million is roughly...

0.9%.

Less than 1%.

Now before somebody turns this into a theological argument, I'm not saying Revelation teaches that only 0.9% of Jewish people—or 0.9% of humanity—will enter Heaven.

It doesn't.

In fact, Revelation 7:9 immediately describes a multitude so large that no one could number it, coming from every nation, tribe, people, and language.

I'm using the percentage to open your eyes.

Because 0.9% should make you stop.

And then I look at my own posts.

Roughly 2% might engage.

Some stop.

Some read.

Some keep scrolling.

And no, liking my post won't get you into Heaven.

Following me won't save you.

Jesus saves.

But numbers make me think.

How many people are actually stopping long enough to examine their hearts?

How many people hear about God every week and keep scrolling through life?

How many people sit in church but never surrender?

How many people know Scripture but don't live it?

How many pastors can preach salvation but don't know how to love the person standing right in front of them?

Pause.

Look around you.

The person sitting beside you at the restaurant.

The woman crying at church.

Your boss.

Your neighbor.

Your family member you've almost given up on.

The homeless man everybody keeps walking around.

The person smiling online while privately falling apart.

Even the false pastor leading sheep somewhere he isn't going himself.

These are souls.

And life is moving fast.

Way too fast for us to treat eternity casually.

Jesus said:

"For the gate is narrow and the way is hard that leads to life, and those who find it are few." — Matthew 7:14

Read that last word again.

Few.

That's what should open our eyes.

I'm not interested in determining who's going to Heaven and who's going to hell.

That's God's seat.

I'm interested in making sure that while I'm still breathing, I point as many people toward Jesus as I possibly can.

And if everybody else is chasing the crowd...

I'll keep looking for the 1.

Because one person matters.

One broken person matters.

One addict matters.

One unbeliever matters.

One person everybody else gave up on matters.

One soul matters.

So who is joining me?

Who is willing to walk the narrow road when everybody else chooses the wide one?

Who is willing to love when hatred is easier?

Forgive when revenge feels better?

Serve when nobody is watching?

Follow Jesus when following the world would be easier?

I know where I'm trying to be.

Among the few.

And if I see you walking that narrow road too...

I'll happily see you there.

Daily Commitment
Surrender is a daily choice. Following Christ requires a decision to place His desires above our own and trust His direction even when it is challenging.
Every day provides a new opportunity to lay aside selfish ambitions, fears, and distractions in order to walk closely with God. Taking up our cross means willingly embracing obedience, faith, and perseverance, even when the path is difficult. As we consistently choose God's will over our own, our hearts are transformed, our faith grows stronger, and we become more like Christ. Daily surrender is not about losing freedom; it is about finding true purpose, peace, and fulfillment in Him.
Ask yourself each morning: “Lord, how can I honor You today?” Small acts of obedience, kindness, forgiveness, and trust become powerful expressions of surrender that shape your spiritual journey over time.

The Fruit of the Spirit 🍇✨

Paul tells us in Galatians 5:22–23 about nine qualities that should be evident in our lives when we are walking according to God’s ways:

❤️ Love
😊 Joy
🕊️ Peace
⏳ Patience
🤍 Kindness
🌿 Goodness
🙏 Faithfulness
🌸 Gentleness
💗 Self-Control

Think about the fruit on a tree. It isn’t there for the tree to consume. It’s there for others to receive.

The same is true with the fruit of the Spirit in our lives. It’s not just for us. It’s for the people around us.

We are called to love one another.
To have joy with one another.
To live in peace with one another.
To be patient, kind, gentle, faithful, and good to one another.

Our lives should produce fruit that others can experience. 🌿

Don’t just say you walk with God. Let your fruit speak for you.

“By their fruit you will recognize them.”
— Matthew 7:16

Let's bless the Lord on this Wonderful Wednesday 16:3 Family! Have a BLESSED day everyone!!! 🙌🥰🙌🙏💯

Many years ago despite God repeatedly warning me through his still small voice,  other people, and common sense. I went down the wrong road in life and did something really wrong.  Got in trouble for it, and for a long time felt like it was something that defined me. Although I never did that again, I always felt the guilt.  God shared with me Romans 5:17, He told me I have more grace than I will ever need. I received that,  and spoke of God's grace to my wife often. It wasn't received,  eventually she left.  She has since passed.  I buried myself in work, I took the gifts and calling God gave me,  and buried them in the ground.  God forgave me. Told me I had more grace than I will ever need. But I didn't forgive me. I worked ever Sunday,  so no church,  but I had Christian radio so I heard music all day. Those songs have their basis in God's word, so he kept me all those years of no church. All those years his grace was evident.  He always provided for me, saved me from harm in a very bad accident,  brought me through heart and breathing issues.  He graced me like he said he would.  One day after a close friend died, I heard him tell me to "get off the sidelines. " I'll never forget that day. By then my schedule allowed me to go to church, I just didn't go. But when he said  get off the sidelines, I knew what that  meant. Go back to church,  get involved,  take that gifting and calling out of the ground and get to work.  Love others, give, teach, pray, serve. You don't need a pulpit to teach.  Talk to people one on one. He kept telling me no one puts a candle under a bushel,  but on a candlestick that it may give light to all in the house. Took me awhile to find where I was supposed to be but he got me there. I know I'm where I'm at is his plan, and I'm back involved.  The past still nagged me though. Then although I rarely used FB, I started looking more often. In my feed was these posts from this guy Jeremy Mills... Ok, I read em,  next thing you know I'm going to FB more often,  now to read these posts from the brother.  So when that open forum that he just put up a few days ago I told my story and the nagging past guilt.  So his response was. Your identity is not found in your worst day. It is found in the cross. Oh. I used to feel defined by that day, but I never said that to anyone.  The Lord has been telling me in other ways too, but when our brother Chico said your identity is not in your worst day, but in the cross. Ya, that was the final nail. Thank you brother Chico. Thank you Lord. He never gave up on me.  He never quit pursuing me.  Who does that? Only God. He's no respector of persons. What he does for me he will do for you. Wherever you find yourself,  even "if I make my bed in hell, thou art there." God is right there with you and willing to pull you out, you just have to let him. He died on the cross and rose from the dead for all of us. You just have to receive Him.  Don't be your lord like I did. Do what he says, life is easier.
Heavenly Father I ask you to bless everyone on 16:3 tonight. Whatever they are going through that they have faith in you.  That they continue to see you first.  Ask this in your name Amen and amen.

Welcome to Day 3 of our devotion series:

💌 *Letters From God to Your Heart*

*Day 3: My Dear Child… Don't Be Afraid*

📖*Isaiah 41:10**

*"So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you and help you; I will uphold you with My righteous right hand."*

Perhaps today...

...you're carrying a fear that no one else knows about.

Perhaps you're worried about your health.

- Your family.
- Your finances.
- Your future.

Or maybe you're afraid of what tomorrow might bring.

Before fear has another opportunity to speak to your heart today, listen to My voice.

My dear child,

- I know what frightens you.
- I know the thoughts that keep you awake at night.
- I know the questions you are afraid to ask.

Nothing about your life is hidden from Me.
You do not have to pretend to be strong all the time.

Bring your fears to Me.

I am not disappointed by your weakness.
- I draw near to those who trust Me.

Remember, fear looks at the size of the problem.
- Faith looks at the greatness of God.

The storm you are facing may seem overwhelming, but it is not greater than My power.

- The uncertainty you feel has not changed My promises.
- The future may be unknown to you...
- But it has never been unknown to Me.

I am already in your tomorrow.

Where you see uncertainty...
- I see purpose.

Where you see obstacles...
- I see opportunities for My faithfulness to be revealed.

So don't let fear become the loudest voice in your life.
- Let My promises speak louder.

- When you feel anxious, remember that I am with you.
- When you feel weak, remember that I am your strength.
- When you feel alone, remember that I will never leave you.

Walk forward today, not because you know what tomorrow holds, but because you know the One who holds tomorrow.

Trust Me.
I will never let go of your hand.

❤️ *Today's Heart Check:*

✅ What fear have I been holding on to instead of giving to God?
✅ Am I allowing fear to shape my decisions, or am I trusting God's promises?
✅ How can I choose faith over fear today?

🙏 *Prayer*

*Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding me that I never have to face life's challenges alone. When fear begins to rise within me, help me to hear Your voice above every anxious thought. Strengthen my faith, calm my heart, and remind me that You are already in every tomorrow I fear. Help me to trust You completely, knowing that You are always with me. In Jesus' name, Amen.*

*Truth to Hold On To Today:*

*"Fear may knock at your door, but it does not have to live in your heart. The God who walks beside you is greater than anything that stands before you."*

Have a blessed Tuesday, everyone. Whatever you are facing today, remember that you do not walk alone. God's presence goes with you, His strength upholds you, and His perfect love drives out fear. Walk confidently, knowing that the One who holds your future is holding your hand today. 💛🙏🏽
